paragraphs.source_en: The distribution of images of mouflon and antelope in the region is not uniform. In the lower mountains of the Algerian Tadrart and the Tadrart Acacus their frequency is almost equal to other animal species, whilst their highest occurrence is attested on the Tassili Plateau. Could the altitude have influenced this situation? With the mouflon and antelope's natural habitat being high in the mountains, they would have been particularly numerous in the Tassili and consequently they would have been depicted here more frequently. On the other hand, excavations (Barich 1987; Cremaschi & Di Lernia 1998) have revealed the abundance of mouflon remains in the Acacus and its lower surroundings, confirming that the distribution of mouflon in rock art does not follow the distribution of these animals in the Central Sahara.

paragraphs.source_en: The images of mouflon and antelope on the Tassili Plateau were clearly connected to this area but for what reason? An explanation may be the possible special status of the Plateau as the highest mountains in the region, possessing the greatest number of shelters. For this reason the Plateau would become the most important image-making area which seems to be confirmed by the fact that it contains not only the majority of all Round Head paintings, but also all characteristic Round Head elements not present in the lower mountains. Since the mouflon and antelope were two fundamental animals in the Round Head culture, their representation and the possible rituals connected to them might have been restricted to the area of presumed major importance, the Tassili Plateau.
